goal: Make wallet database write failures explicit and either handled or deliberately ignored, instead of silently ignored as before.
Fixes several real bugs where a failed disk write left the wallet reporting success while its in-memory and on-disk state diverged (encryption, passphrase change, transaction records).
reviewability: Not ready to review as final: marked needs-rebase and still draft with active force-pushes as of the last update.
The underlying design (treat DB write failures as catastrophic corruption) is settled by the author against reviewer pushback, so the remaining work is code-level review once rebased.
agreement: Three concept ACKs (l0rinc, rkrux, jeanpablojp) with no concept objections.

jeanpablojp raised several concrete scenarios where the new failure handling could regress behavior (skipped backups, orphaned wallet-tx entries, descriptor cache/disk mismatch); achow101 rejected each with a stated rationale that write failures should be treated as catastrophic, and jeanpablojp has not pushed back since.

categories.name: wallet
why: P1 because it closes concrete fund-safety and consistency gaps: encryption and passphrase-change previously reported success while the master key write failed, leaving old and new passphrases inconsistent on disk versus memory.
Also fixes silent data loss paths in transaction and descriptor-key writes that the commit messages describe as retry-breaking or state-publishing-before-commit bugs.

result.summary: This PR marks all WalletBatch read/write/erase/transaction methods [[nodiscard]] and updates every call site to either handle the failure or explicitly document why it is being ignored. Along the way it fixes several bugs where a failed database write left the wallet's in-memory state diverged from disk: encryption and passphrase-change previously reported success despite a failed master-key write, and several key/descriptor writes could be silently dropped. It also changes Unlock/ChangeWalletPassphrase to return util::Expected<void, WalletError> so callers (RPC, GUI) get specific error codes instead of a bare bool, and adds a reusable fault-injecting SQLite wallet database for tests.
result.problem: Many wallet database write failures were previously ignored, so a disk write failure could leave the wallet reporting success while its live state and the on-disk state diverged, risking corruption, lost passphrase changes, or unretryable failures. This affects any wallet user whose disk fills up or whose database write otherwise fails during a sensitive operation like encryption or passphrase change.

open_concerns: jeanpablojp: BackupWallet now skips the actual file copy when WriteBestBlock fails, removing the backup you'd most want right when the database starts failing; author disagreed, treating any write failure as a signal that a backup should not be trusted.

jeanpablojp: IncOrderPosNext failure path can leave a mapWallet entry with no order position, suggesting a specific fix; author says this is an intentional crash-on-corruption path, not something to repair gracefully.

jeanpablojp: TopUpWithDB can throw after updating in-memory descriptor cache range but before persisting it, producing a wallet that fails to reopen for xpub-cache-per-index descriptors; author replied 'what retry?' and reiterated write failures are catastrophic.

jeanpablojp: returning DBErrors::CORRUPT for a version-write failure during load may mislabel a full-disk condition as corruption; author says any write failure is treated as corruption regardless of cause.
resolved_concerns: jeanpablojp's request to remove explanatory comments in test/wallet/test/util.h; author said such comments are unnecessary, no further pushback.

result.card: This draft PR marks all WalletBatch operations [[nodiscard]] and fixes the resulting fallout: several places where a failed database write previously left the wallet reporting success while its in-memory and on-disk state diverged, notably encryption and passphrase-change publishing new key state before the write or transaction commit succeeded. Author achow101 states in commit messages that these are real fund-safety bugs, e.g. 'the old passphrase remains on disk' after a failed master-key write, and reviewer jeanpablojp independently found further edge cases (orphaned transaction records, descriptor cache diverging from disk on write failure) that achow101 addressed by asserting write failures should always be treated as unrecoverable corruption rather than retried. Three reviewers gave concept ACKs and no one has disputed the goal, though the specific failure-handling philosophy drew pushback that the author rejected with rationale and the critic has not re-raised. The PR is flagged needs-rebase and still in active force-push churn, and it explicitly depends on the still-open #35752 (encryption transaction atomicity) landing first. It is central to the wallet category's core concern of fund safety and database corruption handling.
